subject: BlueCrest RFP: Key Custody, BYOK & TLS Controls - consolidated answers

Subject: Follow-up: technical clarifications on key custody and TLS

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the RFP materials — a couple of technical clarifications from our security team before we complete our evaluation: 

1) BYOK / HSM model: Can Redwood support customer-held root keys in customer-managed HSMs (cloud or on-prem) such that Redwood never has exportable plaintext root material? If so, what HSM integrations/protocols are supported (KMIP, PKCS#11, CloudHSM connectors)? Any limitations we should be aware of?

2) Key rotation: describe your recommended rotation cadence for KEKs and DEKs, and whether rotations can be done without service downtime. Do you support dual-wrapping during rollovers?

3) TLS and ciphering: Please confirm minimum TLS version supported and provide the cipher suite list you recommend for compliance with our standards (PCI/ISO).

We may also need an attestation PDF enumerating the BYOK workflow and controls for our procurement review. Can you send a consolidated response by EOD 2027-10-20?

Best,
Samantha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Follow-up: technical clarifications on key custody and TLS

Vanessa / Rishi — draft consolidated answers below. I pulled ops and product notes; Rishi please confirm the HSM/crypto details I flagged. Attachments: redwood_byok_attestation_v2.pdf (one-page workflow + controls), key_rotation_schedule.csv (example schedule), tls_cipher_list.txt (recommended cipher list).

--- consolidated answers (for BlueCrest) ---
1) BYOK / HSM model
- Short answer: Yes — Redwood supports BYOK where customer root/KEK material remains in customer-managed HSMs or cloud HSM services and is never exported in plaintext by Redwood.
- Integrations supported: KMIP for enterprise HSMs, PKCS#11 for on-prem HSM appliances, and native connectors for major cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM / Key Vault HSM-protected keys via Azure Key Vault HSM, and GCP CloudHSM). We also support wrap/unwrap via customer-provided KMIP endpoints and PKCS#11 signing/encrypting operations where the private key material stays within the HSM.
- Operational note: For on-prem HSMs behind customer firewalls, we require a network-facing KMIP proxy or an agreed connector; air-gapped HSMs are supported via an offline import procedure (documented in the attestation).
- Limitations: Some legacy HSMs with proprietary transport may require a partner gateway; bring-your-own-HSM onboarding lead time varies (typical 2-6 weeks depending on access).

2) Key rotation and rollovers
- Recommended cadence: KEK (key-encrypting keys) — default 12 months; DEK (data-encryption keys) — rotated on access pattern triggers or 90–180 days depending on sensitivity. We provide configurable policies per-tenant.
- Zero-downtime rotations: Supported. Redwood uses dual-wrap (old and new KEK) and a staged rollout of wrapped DEKs to ensure active tokens remain decryptable during the rollover window. Rolling rotations are handled by the control plane so no application downtime is required.
- Rotation mechanics: We support both scheduled automatic rotations and on-demand rotations initiated via API/console. Re-wrap operations can be executed in-place; for massive key populations we offer batch re-wrap tooling and a throttled background job system.

3) TLS and cipher suites
- Minimum TLS version: TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 preferred for new deployments.
- Recommended cipher suites: See attached tls_cipher_list.txt. High-level guidance: ECDHE key exchange, AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs, forward secrecy enabled, and disable RSA key exchange and CBC-mode ciphers. We publish current cipher lists in the product docs and maintain a hardened baseline matching industry compliance (PCI/ISO/NIST).

4) Evidence and attestation
- Provided evidence: attached one-page BYOK attestation (redwood_byok_attestation_v2.pdf) outlines the workflow, roles, access controls, and logging evidence we can share with auditors.
- Audit logs: We retain key operation logs (wrap/unwrap, import, rotation events) per customer with configurable retention policies; event-level proofs can be exported for SOC2 or procurement review.

Please review technical phrasing, Rishi, and confirm HSM connector naming and any addendum re: FIPS/HSM certification.

Thanks,
Marissa
Technical Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Follow-up: technical clarifications on key custody and TLS

Marissa / Vanessa — quick confirmations and small clarifications below; insert into the customer-facing doc where appropriate.

- FIPS / certifications: We integrate with FIPS 140-2 level 2/3 validated HSMs commonly provided by AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM. For on-prem HSMs, we map to vendor FIPS validation status in the onboarding checklist and will surface required attestation evidence.
- KMIP / PKCS#11 behavior: When using KMIP, Redwood acts as a KMIP client to your KMIP endpoint and performs Create/Wrap/Activate operations; key material never leaves the customer KMS in plaintext. For PKCS#11 we use an HSM-bound connector that performs cryptographic operations inside the module.
- TLS specifics: Our public API endpoints terminate TLS at our edge with TLS1.3 enabled; customers with stricter cipher requirements can request TLS profile customization for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Operational caveat: Air-gapped HSM import requires an escrow procedure and signing of an import manifest; we documented this in redwood_byok_attestation_v2.pdf.

All good to go from my side. I updated the attestation to call out the KMIP request/response traces we can provide under NDA.

Rishi
Senior Applied Crypto Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha / procurement team —

Thanks for the follow-up. Please find our consolidated responses to the three items you raised, plus a short BYOK attestation PDF and two supplemental files attached: redwood_byok_attestation_v2.pdf, key_rotation_schedule.csv (example cadence + migration steps), tls_cipher_list.txt. Highlights:

- BYOK/HSM: Redwood supports customer-held keys in customer-managed HSMs via KMIP, PKCS#11, and cloud HSM connectors (AWS, Azure, GCP). Customer root keys are not exportable in plaintext by Redwood.
- Rotation: We support scheduled and on-demand rotation with a dual-wrap, zero-downtime rollout model. Default KEK cadence is 12 months; DEKs can be policy-driven.
- TLS: TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 preferred. We recommend ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. See attached list for specifics.

Next steps: please confirm whether you want a brief call to review the attestation and any evidence extracts (KMIP traces, audit log samples) under an NDA. If you approve the attestation PDF as-is, we can provide DocuSign or a procurement cover letter; DocuSign reference: DocuSign:0a9f-BC-1189.
